primary_antecedent.title: Boundary Problems for Wave Equations With Grazing and Gliding Rays
locators: Sections 6.3–6.4, decaying and normalized Airy mapping
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent normal-integrated Fourier proof of the growing-mode weighted upper estimate, two-mode H1 construction, smooth equation errors and actual weak boundary traces.

source_correspondence: The operator uses the actual real variable-coefficient CAA phase and finite matrix amplitudes. The domain consists of measurable frequency coefficients with the exact polynomial Ai and polynomial-plus-exponential Bi weights. No unsupported multiplication in the physical input variable is introduced.

The Fourier normal-operator proof integrates each amplitude column in the normal variable before a frequency supremum. Tangential integration by parts, normal Cauchy–Schwarz and the proved Schur estimate give a complete uniform bound without frequency amplitude derivatives.

The boundary layer and oscillatory cutoffs retain their exact overlap. The oscillatory region lies in a convex frequency half-cone on which the mixed phase matrix is uniformly invertible. Only one frequency derivative is used; no invalid exotic symbol calculus is invoked.

Both exact oscillatory Bi branches have all differentiated amplitude bounds. After one output derivative, their normalized squared normal majorant is q^(-1/2), which is integrable. Every cutoff derivative and finite matrix factor is retained.

The growing layer estimate includes all tangential chain-rule factors, the first output derivative, the boundary endpoint scale and the entire remaining interval. The latter has a fixed exponential gap that absorbs its polynomial factors. The normal Jacobian gives precisely lambda^(4/3).

The earlier sharp Ai mapping is extended to global polynomial coefficient inputs by an explicit compact input cutoff and a fully smoothing, rapidly decreasing off-support kernel. This step is not asserted for the exponential coefficient norm.

Frequency truncations converge in the actual H1 energy norm. The flat caustic residual gives a smooth Ai equation error with every differentiated bound. The exact Bi decomposition through the two normalized Airy modes retains the same, unconjugated, matrix amplitudes and gives smooth errors from their H1/2 coefficient bounds.

The complete differentiated output cutoff error is retained. Smooth equation error is claimed only where the cutoff is one. Coefficient-space completeness is distinguished from closed range, injectivity and representation of all solutions.

The four exact boundary coefficient inequalities give the value and conormal rows in H1/2 and H(-1/2). The normal coefficient, all complex matrix lower terms, order of factors and differentiated output cutoff are preserved.

The original left-coefficient energy form and its signed Green identity are derived. H1 convergence, smooth equation-error convergence, and the actual normal graph trace identify the weak conormal. The earlier explicit trace right inverse provides the stated alternative uniqueness argument.

Three solved exercises compute the failure of interchanging a normal integral and a supremum, the exact affine exponential energy scale and endpoint constant, and the full complex Robin row and weak sign. Thirty-three finite exact checks assist the analytic proof.
All 325 formulas and 39 numbered displays parse. The original figure distinguishes exact cutoff boundaries from illustrative unit-mass exponential densities.

The general weighted reverse estimate and complete variable-coefficient two-mode representation remain unfinished. General manifold scalar observation assembly and all remaining HIII21/23/24 and HIV25/26 obligations remain active. Required human foundation proofs remain external.
